subject: Model shortlist + context budget for FinLytics onboarding
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marino <elena@finlytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model shortlist + context budget for FinLytics onboarding

Hi Elena / FinLytics team —

Following our kickoff, attaching the usage sample you sent and a concise shortlist + context sizing recommendation for implementation planning. The goal here is to propose a small number of model variants we can start serving during the initial 3-month pilot, with token and context budgets so engineering can provision Dedicated or Hosted capacity.

Quick summary:
- Workload: document summarization + Q&A over customer support transcripts (avg input length ~1.2k chars, median 450 tokens).
- Expected concurrency during pilot: 12–20 QPS peak for the support assistant flow (bursting to ~35 QPS during daily peaks).
- Monthly token projection (pilot): 60M input tokens, 90M output tokens (150M total).

Proposed shortlist (attached PDF compares latency/cost estimates):
1) Llama-3-8b-q4f — lowest latency and cost for short responses; good for high-throughput chunks; 4k context is sufficient for ~70% of queries.
2) Bloomz-7b-instruct — stronger instruction-following where longer context is needed; 8k context preferred for threaded transcripts.
3) RedGem-13b-ks (quantized) — when answer quality and long-context consistency matter; reserve for long-document summarizes and escalation paths.

Context window guidance:
- Start pilot with a mixed routing policy: default to 4k model for fast responses, fall back to 8k/13b for tickets flagged as "long context" by the classifier.
- Cache conversation prefixes for returning users to reduce token spend (we estimate ~25% token savings after 2 weeks of active users).

Action items for the engineering handoff:
- Monica: can you validate these QPS and token numbers against the customer traffic sample?
- Ben: please add any constraints on Dedicated sizing / GPU class we should flag to FinLytics (e.g., need A10 vs. A100 for 13b quantized).
- Elena: confirm if FinLytics wants the pilot to include the escalation path to the 13b variant or keep it gated behind a feature flag.

Attachments: finlytics-usage-sample.csv (csv, 48KB), proposed-shortlist-comparison.pdf (5 pages)

Thanks — I left margin notes in the PDF for the tradeoffs.

—

Thanks Mina — quick pass from the traffic sample:

- Peak concurrency checks out at ~30–36 QPS for a 2-hour window (UTC business hours). 12–20 QPS steady is realistic.
- Token breakdown from sample (30-day extract): median input tokens = 420, 75th = 980, 95th = 3,400. That suggests a 4k context will cover ~95% of queries, but the 95th percentile pushes into the 8k range when we include conversation history.

Some notes on provisioning:
- If we expect bursty peaks (~35 QPS) and want 99th percentile latency < 700ms for the 8k route, recommend reserving Dedicated nodes with at least 2x A40-equivalent GPU (or 1x A100 for cost-efficient batch throughput) for the 13b when in fallback mode.
- Caching: the 25% token savings is plausible, but depends on how much of the prefix is stable. For support transcripts, we saw 30–40% prefix stability in earlier customers.

Questions:
1) What SLA for tail latency is FinLytics targeting for the initial pilot?
2) Does FinLytics want us to pre-warm KV cache for returning customer sessions?

I added a short spreadsheet tab with percentile token counts and a suggested monthly token cap to keep cost predictable.

—Monica

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Elena Marino <elena@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model shortlist + context budget for FinLytics onboarding

Looping in my infra notes — high level recommendations for the shortlist and the implementation plan:

- Llama-3-8b-q4f: ideal for default route. On a single A10-class GPU we can sustain ~120 tokens/sec for this model with optimized kernels; 4k contexts are inexpensive and enable dense batching. Good for the majority of quick Q&A.

- Bloomz-7b-instruct (8k): choose a 2-GPU Dedicated pool for the pilot if you expect >=20 sustained QPS on the 8k path; otherwise use hosted with autoscaling and conservative burst limits. Latency target: 700–900ms p95 with batching of small requests.

- RedGem-13b-ks (quantized): quantized 13b costs ~2.5x tokens of 8b in GPU time but yields notably better long-form consistency. For cost control:
  * Gate this behind a feature flag and route only tickets flagged by classifier + manual escalation.
  * Use progressive rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 100% as we confirm quality and tail latency.

Sizing sketch for pilot (30-day):
- Expected total tokens: 150M (as Mina estimated).
- If 70% served by 4k 8b model, 20% by 8k 7b, 10% by 13b — rough GPU-hours: 4k (8b): 160 GPU-hours, 8k (7b): 120 GPU-hours, 13b (quantized): 90 GPU-hours.

Notes for procurement: if FinLytics wants Dedicated SLA with predictable latency, they should commit to a monthly reserved GPU capacity (we can translate GPU-hours into a small reserved footprint for the pilot). I’ll prepare two capacity options (minimal reserve vs burstable).

—Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks everyone — this is super helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. A few quick confirmations: 

- We want the pilot to include the 13b escalation path but behind a feature flag; we will start with 5% rollout.
- SLA: aim for p95 < 800ms on the default 4k path; we understand higher tail on the 13b fallback.
- Please prepare the two capacity options (reserve vs burstable). Procurement will review the GPU-hour translation and the month-by-month cost.

Let’s keep the meeting on Friday at 10am PT to review the capacity options and finalize the scope.

Best,
Elena
